surfaces.name: Kandev web application (browser, incl. phone browser)

claims.answer: Browser is the primary client (served at localhost:38429, also reachable from phones over VPN/tunnel); Tauri desktop ships macOS arm64/x64, Linux x64/arm64 and Windows x64 installers; kandev launcher CLI runs and manages the backend; no native mobile app or editor extension exists in this release.

desktop_os.answer: Tauri desktop installers ship for macOS arm64/x64, Linux x64/arm64 and Windows x64; Windows ARM64 has no native artifact.

mobile_apps.answer: No native iOS/Android app in the release artifact list (macOS/Linux/Windows desktop only) and none documented; phones use the browser UI.

browser.answer: The web app is the primary client, served by the backend on localhost:38429 by default.

mobile_browser.answer: Phone browsers reach the same origin over Tailscale/Cloudflare/private VPN with phone task controls and narrow-screen layouts.

cli.answer: The kandev launcher CLI (run/start, ports, service management) plus agentctl runtime helpers ship in every runtime bundle.

editor_extensions.answer: Bounded search of docs and the pinned release (terms: extension, vsix, open-vsx, marketplace extension) finds only the embedded editor/VS Code panel, no installable editor extension.

task_actions.answer: Start, steer, approve, review and resume from browser and phone task controls; desktop adds native notifications without deep-link navigation.

notifications.answer: Desktop native plus browser notifications for turn-finished/needs-answer/failures; web-push and webhook providers are configurable; clicking a desktop notification is not a navigation path.

cross_device_continuity.answer: State lives in the backend database, so any device reaching the origin continues the same tasks; services persist across logout and sessions resume after restarts.

limitations: No installable native mobile app; phones use the browser UI over a private network path.
No editor extension; code editing happens in the embedded editor/panels.
Unsigned macOS/Windows desktop builds need manual OS security bypasses in this release.

claims.answer: About 25 named ACP/CLI harnesses (Claude Code, Codex incl. experimental app-server, Copilot, Gemini, OpenCode, Pi, Cursor, Grok, Antigravity and more) launched with native logins; any CLI can also run via PTY passthrough; per-step profiles allow mixing harnesses in one workflow.

harnesses.answer: Registry lists Auggie, Claude, Codex, Copilot, Gemini, OpenCode, Amp, Qwen, iFlow, Droid, Kilocode, Pi, Cursor, Kimi, Kiro, Qoder, Trae, omp, Devin, Grok, Hermes, Goose, Muse, Antigravity, MiniMax, each usable with a host-supported executable.

model_providers.answer: Models come from the installed CLIs (composer model picker shows the session CLI); Kandev documents no direct model-provider contracts of its own.

custom_adapters.answer: ACP adapters plus bring-your-own TUI passthrough for any CLI and installable plugin remote executors.

session_integration.answer: Kandev launches and controls sessions through ACP/the CLI and its agentctl runtime (native resume or history injection), reusing native CLI logins.

mixed_harness_operation.answer: Agentic workflows mix-and-match agents per step (e.g. plan with one CLI, implement with another, review with a third).

limitations: Model/provider choice is inherited from each CLI rather than contracted directly by Kandev.

claims.answer: Bring your own agent subscription via native CLI login; API keys via executor secrets/env (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY) and PATs for external clients; no Kandev vendor credits, billing or local-model route; multiple profiles hold distinct credentials.

agent_subscriptions.answer: Existing coding-agent subscriptions work through native CLI logins; Kandev sells no tokens and creates no provider accounts.

api_accounts.answer: Provider API keys reach agents via executor secrets/environment (e.g. OPENAI_API_KEY); external MCP/API clients authenticate with personal access tokens.

vendor_credits.answer: No vendor billing, credits or token sale exist in this self-hosted release; bounded search of site, docs and release notes finds no paid surface.

local_models.answer: Bounded search of the agent registry docs and pinned release (terms: ollama, llama, local model, lm studio) finds no local-model route; models arrive via installed CLIs.

account_switching.answer: Separate agent profiles can carry distinct credentials and be chosen per session/step; per-CLI multi-account handling is inherited from the CLI.

vendor_account_requirement.answer: No Kandev account is required; provider accounts/keys for the chosen CLIs are required.

provider_restrictions.answer: Sprites execution accepts provider lifecycle/billing; agent availability follows the host platform and installed CLIs.

limitations: No Kandev-side billing, credits or subscription metering exist.
No first-party local-model support was found.

claims.answer: Install via Homebrew/Scoop/npm, add a local repo, configure an agent profile and start a first task; local and GitHub-backed repos supported; repository-free tasks exist; SSH plus service guides cover own-server onboarding; no managed-cloud path exists.

first_task_setup.answer: Get-started path: install, add a local repository, configure an agent profile keeping Worktree selected, start and review the first task.

no_git.answer: Repository-free tasks exist (repository-less configuration chat; hidden automation runs with no repository).

local_git_without_remote.answer: Repository settings accept existing local Git paths and local executors operate on those checkouts; only push/change-request creation uses origin.

hosted_git.answer: GitHub (incl. GHES/Enterprise Cloud), GitLab (incl. self-managed) and Azure DevOps remote sources with managed contribution tasks.

prerequisite_guidance.answer: Prerequisites are listed (Git, agent-CLI credentials, npm 7+ for the npm channel only, Docker only for Docker profiles) with trust-boundary guidance.

managed_cloud_setup.answer: No vendor cloud or managed compute offering exists; the product runs on user infrastructure and bounded search of site/docs/releases finds no cloud onboarding.

byo_vps_onboarding.answer: Own-server path via SSH executors, systemd/launchd service installs (incl. Linux VPS system mode) and private phone access over Tailscale/Cloudflare/VPN.

limitations: No vendor-managed cloud onboarding exists by design (self-hosted product).

claims.answer: Complete WebSocket action API plus REST /api/v1, versioned Go/npm plugin SDK, external MCP (streamable HTTP + SSE) for create/manage from outside agents, incoming authenticated webhooks and outgoing notification webhooks; launcher CLI covers run/service management.

cli.answer: kandev run/start/service plus agentctl runtime helpers ship in bundles; task create/inspect/steer/stop/review go through the WebSocket/REST/MCP surfaces, not a task CLI.

api.answer: REST /api/v1 routes plus the documented single-/ws JSON action protocol (request/response/notification/error envelope, named error codes) covering boards, tasks, sessions and runs.

sdk.answer: Go/npm plugin SDK (module github.com/kdlbs/kandev/pluginsdk, Serve entrypoint, manifest checker), versioned independently with a published 0.2.1 tag.

mcp_server.answer: External MCP endpoint at /mcp (modern negotiation plus legacy initialize) with SSE compatibility at /mcp/sse and /mcp/message; copyable snippets for popular CLIs.

webhooks.answer: Incoming authenticated webhooks trigger automations; outgoing notification webhooks are a configured provider (10s timeout, SSRF guards) alongside web push.

operations.answer: Create, inspect, steer, stop and review operations exist across WS/REST/MCP; exact-run stop, title snapshots and durable cleanup retry are documented.

authentication.answer: Bearer personal access tokens for programmatic clients; same-origin browser sessions when auth is on; synthetic administrator identity when auth is off.

stability.answer: API paths are versioned (/api/v1) but no published stability or deprecation policy was found in the bounded doc search.

limitations: External MCP intentionally omits stop_task plus live session question/plan/spawn/message tools.
The kandev CLI is a launcher/service manager, not a task-operation CLI.

claims.answer: Workspace MCP definitions (remote, managed npm, existing executables over stdio/HTTP/SSE) selectable per repository/profile/task/session; built-in packages with workspace policy; plugin marketplace plus sideloading; utility agents, custom and saved prompts; MCP/tool policy caveats documented.

mcp_client.answer: Workspace-owned remote, managed-npm and existing-executable MCP definitions selectable additively for repositories, profiles, tasks and sessions.

plugins.answer: Marketplace browse/install/update plus URL/tarball sideloading; management is administrator-scoped; loaded plugin code runs with backend privileges.

custom_tools.answer: Utility agents and custom one-shot helpers, custom/saved prompts, per-session MCP selection and installable plugin tools.

instructions_import.answer: Saved and custom prompts, move-time instruction blocks and workflow prompts are product-managed; agent skills live in experimental Office.

authentication.answer: Integration credentials use the encrypted secret store and narrowest-scope guidance; per-definition MCP authentication detail is not fully established by this pass.

permission_scope.answer: Built-in package scoping (Core required, Configuration opt-in) plus workspace policy that agents cannot self-grant; allow-all baseline caveat applies.

integration_owner.answer: MCP/profile/repository/task selection is product-managed; passthrough sessions inherit the underlying CLI behavior.

limitations: Launch resolution starts from an allow-all baseline overlaid with executor policy, so blank remote policies allow transports.
Passthrough sessions lack full structured chat, task MCP and resumable ACP state.

claims.answer: Desktop is a Tauri shell (Rust launcher, system WebView) over the backend-served SPA; mobile clients are the responsive web app plus a shipped PWA manifest; no native mobile or Electron client exists.

desktop_implementation.answer: Tauri: Rust starts the bundled headless backend on an owned loopback origin inside a system WebView (tauri.conf.json productName Kandev, identifier dev.kandev.desktop).

mobile_implementation.answer: Web/PWA: responsive phone UI served by the backend plus a shipped web manifest (standalone display); no native phone codebase.

hybrids.answer: Tauri native shell hosting the backend-served SPA; backend remains one Go process across channels.

implementation_evidence.answer: Source-inspected tauri.conf.json and PWA manifest plus official architecture and desktop-app docs at the pinned commit.

limitations: No store listing or documented install flow for the PWA manifest.
Unsigned macOS/Windows desktop builds need manual OS bypasses in this release.

claims.answer: Native task creation plus prompt intake (Quick/Config chat), provider issue/MR import and watches from GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Sentry and Azure; Kandev tasks own workflow state while provider links are retained; PR-open/PR-merged triggers shipped, push/CI triggers in progress.

local_creation.answer: New Task flow with searchable workflow, profile, repository and branch controls.

prompt_intake.answer: Prompt-driven intake via Quick Chat, configuration chat and per-task composers with file attachments.

external_import.answer: Issues/work items/MRs from GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Sentry and Azure can be browsed and launched as tasks; watches create tasks from provider events.

chat_git_triggers.answer: GitHub PR-open and PR-merged automations are shipped; push and CI triggers are documented as in-progress stubs.

authoritative_tracker.answer: The Kandev task owns workflow position while provider objects stay linked; Jira copies data rather than keeping a durable two-way association.

stable_ids.answer: Durable Kandev task IDs plus retained provider links (PR/MR numbers, URLs, states surfaced on related-task responses).

sync.answer: Watch polling (with documented caps) and PR/MR lifecycle messages keep states aligned; Azure/Jira/Linear sync is constrained and one-directional in places.

supported_edits.answer: Provider-scoped edits: GitHub checks/reviews/comments, GitLab approvals/discussions, Jira transitions, Linear state changes; Azure arbitrary editing not supported.

external_roundtrips.answer: Submodule PRs stay separate provider workflows and some operations need provider permissions or UI; the task PR panel covers the GitHub path fully.

limitations: Jira launch copies data without a durable association.
GitHub push/CI triggers are coming-soon stubs, not working triggers.

claims.answer: One structured Markdown plan per regular task with Plan panel, version history, compare/revert, plan-mode Implement flow, human and agent (task-MCP) editing, and persistence across restarts; amendment while running is supported via moves and wait steps.

plans.answer: Each task keeps one editable Markdown plan with a dedicated Plan panel and plan mode.

acceptance_criteria.answer: Completion policies, explicit completion gating and plan comments on exact steps exist; a named acceptance-criteria construct was not found.

editors.answer: Humans edit in the panel; agents create/read/update/delete plans through task MCP (passthrough sessions excluded).

revisions.answer: Plan revision history with compare and revert; consecutive writes can coalesce into one revision.

implementation_links.answer: Plan Implement flow continues into sessions with linked repositories and associated PRs; direct plan-step-to-commit links are not established.

amendment.answer: Plans and moves can change while work runs (moves queue behind running agents with options preserved); human wait steps gate auto-advance.

restart_persistence.answer: Plans persist in SQLite and survive backend restarts with lazy session recovery.

limitations: No explicit acceptance-criteria field; plan comments on steps carry the reviewable detail.
Passthrough-only sessions lack the plan contract.

claims.answer: One-level subtasks with workspace inheritance choice, stored blocker/dependency relations with cycle rejection and a dependency-graph view, WIP-gated moves, and workflow changes that preserve task identity; arbitrary-depth trees and epic promotion are Office-only in-progress work.

epics.answer: No epic backlog entity exists; bounded search of task/workflow docs and the pinned release (terms: epic, initiative, theme) finds only workflow groupings.

hierarchy.answer: Regular kanban supports parent plus direct children through UI and MCP; arbitrary-depth trees are Office-only in progress.

blockers.answer: Blocked_by relations are stored, cycle-checked and block automated starts, with related-task inspection; the full create/edit/filter picker is Office UI.

readiness.answer: A blocked task is not started by any automated path and fires once predecessors succeed; chained creates build chains.

enforcement.answer: Blocked tasks are held from auto-start and moves re-check routing, permissions, WIP and session state; display-level enforcement beyond holds is not established.

state_propagation.answer: Direct-child completion feeds workflow events and actions; no roll-up or epic-level propagation exists.

task_to_epic.answer: No promotion path from task to epic exists; bounded search finds only subtask creation and workflow changes that preserve identity.

identity_retention.answer: Changing a workflow keeps task identity, description, repositories and existing conversations, with optional per-task profile mapping.

workflow_constraints.answer: WIP/pull controls, fixed per-step profiles and guard-checked transitions constrain flow; scoped exceptions are possible via move-with-options and profile mapping.

limitations: No epic entity and no grow-a-task-into-an-epic path.
Blocker/dependency create/edit/filter pickers are Office UI; regular kanban surfaces stored relations without a complete editing path.
Arbitrary-depth trees are in progress.

claims.answer: Workflow/custom prompts, per-task documents with revisions, retained session conversations with resume-time history injection, utility-agent summaries for handoff, and takeover that preserves context; no product-managed cross-session memory outside experimental Office.

instructions.answer: Repository instruction settings, workflow prompts, custom/saved prompts and move-time instruction blocks.

skills.answer: Utility agents and custom one-shot helpers are shipped; named agent skills are experimental Office surface.

project_docs.answer: Per-task documents with revision history (plans, specs, notes, reviews); no workspace-level persistent product-spec store outside Office documents in progress.

memory.answer: Session history persists and is re-injected on resume or summarized for handoffs; no managed long-term memory beyond experimental Office.

scope.answer: Workspace/task/session scoping for prompts, MCP packages and secrets is documented; cross-workspace memory scoping is not established.

provenance.answer: Message attribution, human-action attribution and utility-agent summary labeling exist; full source provenance for injected context is not established.

correction.answer: Plan compare/revert, thread comments on extracts and editable prompts allow correction; managed stale-context controls are not established.

deletion.answer: Session deletion, context reset, prompt/profile/document deletion flows with confirmations exist.

freshness.answer: Watch polling and provider re-checks refresh linked state with documented caps; no staleness model for injected memory.

takeover_continuity.answer: Colleague takeover (reassign plus continue) and agent handoff preserve task, session history, decisions and artifacts.

limitations: Managed cross-session/cross-harness memory is Office-only in progress.
Generated summaries can omit constraints or decisions.

claims.answer: Agents work with full repo checkouts and provider-linked context (issues, PRs, Sentry) while Kandev itself provides diff/review surfacing, divergence detection and human gates; no product-owned code index, semantic retrieval, citation model or spec-conformance enforcement exists.

code_search.answer: File editor/tree/terminal search plus agent-CLI search over full checkouts; no product search index.

indexing.answer: Bounded search of backend services and docs (terms: embedding, vector, semantic index, repository index) finds no product-owned indexing service.

external_knowledge.answer: Provider objects (issues, PRs, Sentry events) and web links are brought into task context; general web knowledge is agent-side.

multimodal_inputs.answer: Image/file attachments on answers and prompts (bounded counts and sizes) delivered to agent execution as readable paths.

freshness.answer: Watch polls and provider re-resolution refresh linked state; comparison bases are re-checked before mutating actions.

access_scope.answer: Per-task repository attachments with base/checkout branches bound what agents and reviewers see.

api_retrieval.answer: Backend reads provider APIs for issues/PRs/checks within workspace scope; agent-side retrieval is CLI capability.

citations.answer: Canonical PR URLs in lifecycle templates and anchored plan/thread comments; no formal citation model.

conflict_detection.answer: Divergent task-vs-PR history detection with neutral wording and compare flows; no semantic conflict detection.

review_enforcement.answer: Human gates plus provider required-check enforcement on merge; agent assertions alone never satisfy a gate.

limitations: No product-owned semantic index or embeddings service; retrieval is agent-CLI capability plus file panels.
No spec-conformance enforcement at review time.

claims.answer: Full native task lifecycle on kanban/pipeline boards (create, edit, discuss, assign, search, archive, reopen, workflow views, dispatch control, task/session separation, durable states) without any external tracker; labels and full dependency editing are Office-surface in progress.

create.answer: New Task flow with workflow, profile, repository and branch selection.

edit.answer: Title, prompt, workflow moves, profile mapping and repository attachments are editable.

discuss.answer: Task conversations, plan/thread comments on exact extracts and message threads.

prioritize.answer: Workflow ordering, WIP rules and Needs-you/Queue surfacing prioritize; no dedicated priority field is established.

label.answer: Label storage exists but catalogs, pickers and filters are Office-surface in progress per Feature Status.

assign.answer: Independent human assignee and agent assignee rows with Assign-to-me.

filter.answer: Board and view filters exist; label-based filtering is Office-surface.

archive.answer: Archive/unarchive with async runtime cleanup and phone confirmation sheets.

reopen.answer: Unarchive restores tasks; deleted-task recovery is not claimed.

project_epic_views.answer: Kanban and pipeline views per workflow with columns, counts and PR badges.

idea_parking.answer: Backlog steps and destinations without auto-start let ideas wait without dispatching agents.

explicit_dispatch.answer: Manual start, auto-start preferences and explicit step-move dispatch with previews.

task_session_separation.answer: Tasks own workflow state while multiple named sessions attach to one task environment.

metadata.answer: Assignees, repositories, workflow position and states are first-class; label/dependency metadata editing is Office-surface.

durable_states.answer: Workflow steps, archive state and Done completion persist in the database.

external_tracker_requirement.answer: No external tracker is required; integrations are optional attachments.

limitations: Label catalogs, pickers and filters live on the flagged Office surface, not regular kanban.
Dependency create/edit/filter pickers are Office UI; regular kanban surfaces stored relations only.

claims.answer: Agents read, create, update, move, link and report on the same durable task IDs humans use through documented task-MCP tools, with attribution, workspace policy and cycle/permission guards; direct stop and cross-task message tools are scoped accordingly.

shared_ids.answer: Agents operate on the same durable task/session IDs and fields humans see.

read.answer: List/inspect workspaces, workflows, tasks, related tasks, conversations and plans.

create.answer: Create top-level tasks and subtasks with optional auto-start, inheritance choice and dependency declarations.

update.answer: Move steps, attach branches, adjust diff bases, archive/delete with handoff prompts and completion signals.

claim.answer: Agent assignment rows record ownership; claiming is assignment, not an exclusive lock (takeover reassigns without locking).

assign.answer: Agent assignee rows plus human Assigned-to rows are settable independently.

state_changes.answer: Move tasks across steps and emit explicit step-completion signals gating auto-advance.

dependencies.answer: Declare blocked_by at creation or add/remove relations later; cycles rejected; blocked tasks held from automated starts.

children.answer: Subtask creation with inherited or new workspaces; direct-child completion feeds workflow events.

results.answer: Completion signals with summary/handoff/blockers, session-shared walkthroughs and PR associations.

human_visibility.answer: Boards, sessions, review panels and lifecycle messages reflect agent writes to humans.

attribution.answer: Agent-spawned sessions carry sender/route attribution; human actions record the acting person.

permissions.answer: Workspace policy and package scoping apply; agents cannot self-grant Configuration packages; ambient-token caveats documented.

conflicts.answer: Cycle rejection and unsafe-reuse refusal exist; concurrent file edits may collide by design.

limitations: External MCP omits stop and live session question/plan/spawn/message tools.
Claim semantics are assignment-based; no exclusive agent lock exists.

persistent_requirements.answer: Bounded search of docs and backend (terms: living spec, product spec, persistent requirements, drift) finds only per-task plans and experimental Office documents.

human_edits.answer: No cross-task spec editing surface exists outside per-task documents and Office documents in progress.

agent_edits.answer: Agent plan tools are task-scoped; no agent-editable cross-task spec exists.

revisions.answer: Revision history exists for per-task plans/documents only, not for a cross-task specification.

approvals.answer: Approval flows are task/PR-scoped (review/approval stages); no spec approval rules exist.

implementation_links.answer: No requirement-to-task/implementation link model was found.

later_retrieval.answer: No retrieval of persistent specs into later tasks is documented or implemented.

drift_detection.answer: No drift detection between specs and implementation exists.

review_integration.answer: Review gates reference tasks and PRs, never a persistent specification.

limitations: Per-task plans/documents are covered under PLAN-02; they do not constitute a living cross-task spec.

claims.answer: Independently running named sessions share a task environment while multiple tasks run in parallel; automation concurrency caps and one-active-run semantics bound load; boards, stats and Inbox expose running, waiting, failed and finished work.

concurrent_sessions.answer: Multiple named sessions attach to one task environment and run concurrently.

concurrent_tasks.answer: Multiple tasks across workflows run and are reviewed in parallel.

quotas.answer: Automation concurrency limits and one-active-run reusable mode exist; no general session quota is documented.

observed_concurrency.answer: Parallel named sessions, parallel tasks and multi-repo fan-out are documented product behavior, not mere tabs.

status_visibility.answer: Boards with step counts, session states, stats workload pages and question Inbox expose running/waiting/failed/finished work.

limitations: No documented global session/task quota beyond automation concurrency and single-run semantics.

claims.answer: Human and agent assignees, automation queues with concurrency limits, compatibility routing for profiles/executors, and cycle guards; ownership is assignment-based with takeover-by-reassign and no exclusive lock or duplicate prevention beyond documented checks.

human_assignment.answer: Human assignee rows with Assign-to-me and unit-based reachability.

agent_assignment.answer: Agent assignee rows per task plus per-step agent profiles and handoff profile choice.

claims.answer: Assignment records ownership; claiming is not an exclusive lock.

queues.answer: Automation runs queue with one-active-run semantics; the workspace coordinator Queue is in-progress behind a flag.

routing.answer: Profile pickers filter to executor-compatible profiles and moves re-check routing/permissions/WIP/session state.

duplicate_prevention.answer: Cycle rejection and workspace_reuse_unsupported refusal; concurrent same-file edits are allowed to collide.

ownership_enforcement.answer: Display plus reassignment; advisory/enforced exclusivity is not established.

limitations: No exclusive ownership lock; a colleague can take over without the holder releasing.
No general duplicate-work prevention beyond cycle checks and unsafe-reuse refusal.

claims.answer: Product task-MCP (spawn/message/stop scoped tools) lets sessions delegate to other sessions with attribution; coordinator-led teams are shipped for kanban delegation while persistent cross-harness Office teams remain experimental.

roles.answer: Primary/spawned session roles, handoff targets and experimental coordinator/participant seats.

model_harness_effort.answer: Per-profile model/flags/permissions and per-step agent selection, including mixed-harness steps.

messages.answer: Targeted task messages queue to running sessions or start idle ones with sender attribution.

results_return.answer: Completion signals, summaries, walkthroughs and shared plans return results to parents/humans.

cross_harness.answer: Per-step mixed providers are shipped; persistent cross-harness Office teams are in progress.

orchestration_owner.answer: Delegation tools are product-owned task MCP; coordinator-led subtask execution is a shipped Done roadmap item.

activation.answer: UI New Agent/handoff plus spawn_session/message tools from inside agents.

authentication.answer: Workspace policy, package scoping and permission checks gate tools; per-tool auth detail beyond policy is not fully established.

live_progress.answer: Chat, tool activity, session states and background-work views expose live progress.

retained_results.answer: Conversations, plans, walkthroughs and review history persist after completion.

followup.answer: Message threads, handoff, reopen and resume continue work after completion.

invocation.answer: Delegation invokes through documented UI and MCP paths, never hidden shell assembly.

limitations: Cross-harness persistent teams, quorum/participant mechanics and Office routines are experimental/in-progress.
External MCP omits spawn/message/stop tools.

claims.answer: Schedule (@every/cron presets), authenticated webhook and GitHub PR triggers create hidden or normal-task runs from the backend with concurrency limits and retry policy; fixed-cron timezones are not honored and push/CI triggers are stubs.

schedules.answer: Manual, @every and cron-preset schedules with per-trigger enablement and timezone field (with the noted limitation).

events.answer: Authenticated webhooks and GitHub PR-open/PR-merged events fire runs; push/CI events are in-progress stubs.

recurring_tasks.answer: Recurring automation runs and experimental Office routines repeat work on schedule.

completion_conditions.answer: Explicit completion gating and one-active-run semantics exist; no rich condition language is established.

scheduler_location.answer: Triggers dispatch from backend automation runs, independent of any open client.

overlaps.answer: Concurrency limit plus one-active-run reusable mode serialize overlap; general overlap policy beyond that is not established.

retries.answer: Saved retry policies, generic retry admission and dynamic-routing retries (experimental) exist.

client_independence.answer: Backend-owned dispatch keeps firing with the client closed; services keep it resident across reboots.

limitations: Fixed cron timezone values are not honored; prefer presets or @every.
GitHub push/CI triggers are coming-soon stubs.
Retry model is policy-based, not a general scheduler guarantee.

claims.answer: Stop/resume/steer (with queued messages), clarification and permission questions with attachments, Inbox history, failure alerts and desktop notifications, plus retained SQLite history; generic pause and escalation chains are not established.

pause.answer: Stop plus human wait-step gating achieve pause-like control; a dedicated regular-session pause is not established.

stop.answer: Stop sessions and exact-run automation stops with async runtime teardown.

resume.answer: Resume sessions including lazy recovery after backend restart (native resume or history injection).

steer.answer: Message running sessions (queued for next turn) or idle ones immediately; move-with-options redirects work.

notifications.answer: Turn-finished/needs-answer/failure alerts via desktop, browser, web-push and webhook channels.

pending_decisions.answer: In-box clarification/permission questions with history; experimental coordinator Needs-you surface.

escalation.answer: No escalation chain (manager routing beyond experimental coordinator holds) was found in bounded doc/code search.

visible_errors.answer: Error states, failed sessions, lifecycle messages and background-work history surface visibly.

chat_terminal_parity.answer: Structured sessions share chat/files/review; passthrough TUI sessions keep native CLI behavior without product parity.

retained_history.answer: Conversations, plans and review history persist in SQLite across restarts and client changes.

limitations: No generic pause for regular sessions or escalation chain; coordinator pause/holds are experimental.

fleet_fixture.answer: Boards span several workflows with columns, counts and workload stats pages.

parent_child.answer: Subtask links with detachment UI and per-task grouping.

dependencies.answer: Dependency-graph view and stored relations; full editing picker is Office UI.

attention.answer: Question Inbox, PR badges and status strips flag attention; Needs-you/Queue roll-up is in progress.

history.answer: Per-task conversation/plan/review history; workspace-level activity history is Office surface.

workload.answer: Stats workload views by task, agent, project and time.

navigation_errors.answer: Failed cross-step moves surface errors and the card keeps its previous step.

fixture_mode.answer: No product fixture/demo-data mode was found in bounded search of docs and the pinned release (terms: fixture, demo data, sample data).

limitations: No required-review batch queue or cross-epic roll-up outside experimental coordinator/Office.

claims.answer: Quick tasks, subtask-grown scope with identity-preserving workflow changes, templates, configuration-chat natural language, per-agent configuration, in-run move options, live session roles and retained relationships are all shipped; discoverability is docs plus command palette and external auth needs PAT setup.

quick_task.answer: Quick Chat and New Task start single tasks immediately.

growing_epic.answer: Subtasks add scope and workflow changes preserve identity; epic promotion does not exist.

presets.answer: Workflow templates, profile presets, launch presets and saved prompts.

natural_language.answer: Configuration chat creates automations and workflow prompts configure behavior in prose.

agent_configuration.answer: Per-profile model, flags, secrets, permissions and per-step agent assignment with mapping.
